note: The PostScript file operator supplies an input-controlled string whose first decoded byte is NUL; because only len is checked, the non-percent path stores the NUL-prefixed name as a real filename.
The filename length remains nonzero even though the C string view begins with NUL, allowing later open logic to treat it differently from a zero-length name.

code: return open_file(iodev, pfn->fname, pfn->len, file_access, ps, mem);
note: The NUL-prefixed filename and its nonzero length are passed to the default OS open_file implementation.

The stream-open path notices only the leading NUL byte after file_prepare_stream has allocated a stream and buffer, and treats the nonzero-length filename like an empty C string instead of rejecting it or undoing the partially prepared stream.
Success is returned with a prepared but uninitialized stream object whose procedure table and modes were never set by file_init_stream.
The broken stream is still accepted by zfile, receives the original NUL-prefixed filename metadata, and is converted into a PostScript file object.
The bytesavailable operator calls through the uninitialized stream procedure table for the broken file object, producing the target invalid function call/segmentation fault.
